en: The Jātaka: The Fifth Book of Birth Stories,
Chapter on the Arising of Beauty.
8. The Tacasāra Jātaka:
“Falling into the hands of enemies, equipped with nothing but a bamboo core;”
“Your facial complexion is serene;
why do you not grieve?
“Not by grieving or lamenting,”
Even a very small gain is better than nothing;
seeing him grieving and suffering,
his enemies become delighted.
But when a wise person,
knowing how to discern what is beneficial,
does not waver in times of adversity, his enemies become distressed.
Seeing that his face was unchanged from before,
[he thought: "By means of incantations, mantras, well-spoken words,
by offerings, or through family lineage..."
In whatever way and wherever one may find benefit,
in that very way and in that very place should one exert effort.
But when one knows that it is unobtainable, [one should desist].
“Whether by me or by another, this matter must be endured without grieving:
‘What can I do now? Karma is firm.’”
The Tacasāra Jātaka, the eighth.
